verdict.rationale: Amplitude documents a built-in 'Amplitude AI' assistant that lets users ask plain-language questions and get answers across their data without writing SQL or building dashboards, which is a form of task delegation to an in-product AI assistant. However, the story implies broader agentic task delegation (not just Q&A), and the evidence for 'completing tasks' (docs-26) actually describes an embeddable customer-facing agent for the AI-native user's own end-users, not an assistant that performs analyst tasks on their behalf; the deeper AI integrations are mostly funneled through the external MCP server rather than a fully agentic in-product assistant. Missing for 10: evidence of the assistant autonomously executing multi-step analytics tasks (e.g., building dashboards, running experiments) rather than just answering questions, and independent/hands-on validation of its task-completion capability.
